text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Political parties are not my guardian, says President Glafcos Clerides with reference to criticism of Diko leader Spyros Kyprianou at performance as a minister.
- Greek parliament chairman Apostolos Kaklamanis urges caution but not rejection of a new U.S. initiative on Cyprus.

- Greek deputy foreign minister Christos Rozakis arrives for consultations with the Cypriot government to map common positions of the two countries on initiatives from third countries regarding the Cyprus problem.
- First day of the hunting season is marked by accidents and the injury of 24 hunters.

- German foreign ministry document says Cyprus is not ready for European Union accession and distances itself from the official EU position that entry without solving the political problem first is possible.
- British detectives start fresh inquiries into the murder of a Cypriot businessman in London in 1985. Cyprus police deny they have arrested his widow.
- "I won't accept to be guided by party A or party B," says Clerides.
- Radiomarathon in aid of special children starts today and ends tomorrow at midnight.
